cells.tense: Right now you are the one who knows which way you're headed, and you are walking that way on purpose.
cells.ask: Tell one person the heading you've picked and what it's for — not to be agreed with, just to have it heard. Then let them keep theirs.
cells.core:
You know your heading and you're moving by it. That's not a mood you're obeying or a hunch you're hoping holds — it's a choice you made, and the people around you can feel how settled you are in it. What keeps it clean is that you're not pointing at them while you point at it. You let them have their own direction and you keep yours, and the two of you stand side by side instead of one correcting the other.

What this balance is free to feed is the next person who needs the thing you carry shared rather than defended. You can hold your heading without pushing it on anyone, which means what you have goes out as support instead of pressure. Keep choosing it while it's easy, and say out loud what it's feeding — otherwise the quiet part stays quiet, and the people who could draw on it don't learn it's there.

cells.tense: You are already bracing at a future where you have settled this once and for all, and you are trying to write that settlement in ahead of time.
cells.ask: Pick one heading and act on it as it is now, unproven. For a day, don't reopen it or check it against anything else. Let that version steer you.
cells.core:
You can name the direction you're drawn toward, and then you keep checking. There is one more thing that would make the choice safer, one more angle that would show whether this is really it — and the checking has become the relationship, more than the pull itself. A direction doesn't survive being studied like that. The draw you felt at the start is still there, but it now sits behind a question about whether you're allowed to trust it.

What's underneath the testing is that you take in a great deal and you take it in well. Plenty of true things, all of them real. The trouble isn't that you know too much — it's that you've made the choice wait on knowing everything first, and knowing everything isn't arriving. The way back is the same ability in its calm form: something lands and you don't argue with it. You can do that today, in small things, and let that be enough.

cells.tense: You set a direction a while back, and you have been standing at that doorway long after the door closed behind you.
cells.ask: Choose one small direction today — an hour, a call, a route — and let someone you trust hear what you picked before you do it.
cells.core:
There's a direction you haven't taken, and something in you is still back at the point where you could have taken it. The pull you used to feel hasn't gone; what's gone is the pointing. You recognise the direction when someone else names it and you go quiet, because naming yours means standing somewhere, and standing somewhere has felt like too much to ask for a while now.

What's underneath is connection, and what feeds it isn't force. It's the kind of care that doesn't exhaust — tending something small and letting it grow without clutching it. You don't have to decide anything large to restart the current. Pick one thing you can tend without draining yourself, let one person see it, and let the next choice be small too. The pull comes back through practice, not through resolution.

cells.tense: In this very moment you are already steering by a heading you picked, and you describe it as if the steering were happening to you.
cells.ask: Say to one person, plainly: this is the direction I'm going and I chose it. No hedging — one sentence, out loud.
cells.core:
You're already moving in a direction. It's in how you talk about what's ahead, what you make room for, what you let slide. You picked that at some point, and the evidence is all over your week. But you describe it as the situation, or the way things are, or what needs doing — as if the pointing were happening somewhere else and you were only reporting on it.

What you take in is real. That's not the problem. The problem is that the one taking it in, and doing the choosing, isn't being counted — not by you, not out loud. The simplest way back is also the plainest, and it's the same strength you already use on other people turned around for a moment: hold your own choice the way you'd hold someone else's, without crushing it or letting it go.

attempts.check: The record says the tense for Too Much is future and the mechanism is diagonal, but it does not license a claim that the person's deliberation is already costing them a specific relationship or that they have turned a particular calling into an object of study — that is the strongest unsupported move in my draft and the reader could reasonably say the inspection is discernment working well, not excess. The ask survives being wrong: naming one direction and stopping the research for 24 hours is useful whether the person is over-examining or simply thorough. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'you're auditing instead of walking' that makes the person feel caught rather than seen; I have cut it. For Too Little, the record allows locating someone behind the present but not saying what happened there, so I have kept the door closed and only said standing at it.
